   Welcome to the Arcadia City Council Meeting!

The City Council encourages public participation, and invites you to share your views on City business.

MEETINGS: Regular Meetings of the City Council are held on the first and third Tuesday of each month at 7:00 p.m.
in City Council Chambers. A full City Council agenda packet with all backup information is available at City Hall and
on the City’s website at www.ArcadiaCA.gov. Copies of individual Agenda Reports are available via email upon request
(CityClerk@ArcadiaCA.gov). Documents distributed to a majority of the City Council after the posting of this agenda
will be available for review at the Office of the City Clerk, 240 W. Huntington Drive, Arcadia, California. Live broadcasts
and replays of the City Council Meetings are on cable television. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in
the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION: Your participate-on is welcomed and invited at all City Council meetings. Time is reserved
at each regular meeting for those in the audience who wish to address the City Council. The City requests that persons
addressing the City Council refrain from making personal, slanderous, profane, or disruptive remarks. Any person
wishing to speak before the City Council may do so using one of the following methods.
  1. In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicate the agenda item number and place it in the Public Comment
  Drop Box, or simply come to the podium when the Mayor asks for those who wish to speak.
  2. Remote Participation: Click on the link or join using the Webinar/Meeting ID or call the established conference
  line.
  PUBLIC COMMENTS: Should be presented during the time designated as “PUBLIC COMMENTS”, for all matters
  on the agenda or not on the agenda. By State law, the City Council may not discuss or vote on items not on
  the agenda. The matter may be referred to staff for appropriate action or response or will be placed on
  the agenda of a future meeting except for public hearing items.

  PUBLIC HEARINGS AND APPEALS: Are items scheduled for which public input is either required or desired.
  Separate and apart from the applicant (who may speak longer in the discretion of the City Council), the allotted
  speaking time is generally determined by the number of speakers, in accordance with the following format: 5
  speakers or less – 5 minutes each; between 6 and 20 speakers – 3 minutes each; between 21 and 50 speakers
  – 2 minutes each; and more than 50 speakers – 1 minute each. The applicant may additionally submit rebuttal
  comments.

AGENDA ITEMS: The Agenda contains the regular order of business of the City Council. Items on the Agenda have
generally been reviewed and investigated by the City Staff in advance of the meeting so that the City Council can be
fully informed about a matter before making its decision.

CONSENT CALENDAR: Items listed on the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine by the City Council and will
be acted upon by one motion. There will be no separate discussion on these items unless a member of the City
Council, Staff, or the public so requests. In this event, the item will be removed from the Consent Calendar and
considered and acted on separately.

DECORUM: While members of the public are free to level criticism of City policies and the action(s) or proposed
action(s) of the City Council or its members, members of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to
the orderly conduct of the proceedings, including but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
audience from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members of the audience from
hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not threaten any person with physical harm or act in
a manner that may reasonably be interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the
meeting are expected to adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race, religious creed,
color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition, marital status, gender, sexual orientation, or
age. The Chief of Police, or such member or members of the Police Department, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-Arms
of the City Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and instructions given by the presiding
official or a majority of the Councilmembers, for the purpose of maintaining order and decorum at the meeting. Any
person who violates the order and decorum of the meeting may be placed under arrest and such person may be
prosecuted under the provisions of Penal Code Section 403 7 or applicable Arcadia Municipal Code section.

The following speakers appeared and expressed their opposition to the proposed removal

Dom Tallerico, Arcadia resident, appeared and questioned why the cross-country course is
an issue for the City; he noted that some of the 1984 Olympics cross-country events were
held in northern San Diego County; he also questioned why work began at Santa Anita Park
before permits were issued; and he announced that he will be reaching out to Highland Oaks

  2 10  09-15-2026
 Burton Brink, Arcadia resident and District 2 Candidate, appeared and spoke about the

regarding his endorsements from the Arcadia Police Officers’ Association and the Arcadia
Firefighters’ Association; and stated that, if elected, he would support residents, businesses,
and first responders.

Alpha Biz participated remotely and commented on Steve Rhee’s candidacy for District 5
after previously running for District 4 in 2024; he expressed concerns regarding Mr. Rhee
seeking office in different districts; and he stated that candidates should demonstrate a
commitment to serving in the district they seek to represent.

Meeting Attendee C participated remotely and commented on Steve Rhee’s candidacy for
District 5 after previously running for District 4 in 2024; the speaker questioned his
commitment to District 5; and stated that the election should not just be about campaigning,
but about commitment, consistency, and accountability.

In response to Mayor Cheng’s inquiries, City Manager Lazzaretto clarified that since the last
City Council meeting, Santa Anita Park requested that the City pause its review of the
proposed oak tree removals while alternative options and designs are explored to preserve
more of the Oak trees; he stated that Santa Anita Park is working with LA28 and the
International Equestrian Federation; and he indicated that he did not know when a revised
application would be submitted.

Regarding the construction work currently underway at Santa Anita Park, City Manager
Lazzaretto clarified that the work is unrelated to the LA28 Olympics and is being conducted
in preparation for the Split Rock Jumping Tour event in November and the Enchant Christmas
event.

Mayor Cheng referenced the City Council’s Rules of Procedure and Decorum, noting that City
Council Members may briefly respond to concerns raised during public comment; he
assured the public that discussions concerning the potential removal of oak trees were
happening transparently and publicly; and he encouraged continued public participation on
the matter.

Council Member Kwan pulled Item 9.c - Professional Services Agreement with Vasquez &
Company LLP for the City’s financial auditing services for separate discussion.

It was moved by Council Member Cao, seconded by Council Member Han, and carried on a
roll call vote to approve Consent Calendar Items 9.a, 9.b, and 9.d through 9.k.

AYES:  Cao, Han, Kwan, Fu, and Cheng

Council Member Kwan requested that City Manager Lazzaretto explain why the City is
entering into an agreement with Vasquez & Company LLP for the City’s financial auditing
services.

City Manager Lazzaretto explained that the item is for the City’s annual financial auditing
services; he stated that on July 21, the City Council considered a similar item and selected
Moss, Levy & Hartzheim LLP; however, following its selection, the firm withdrew from the
engagement, citing concerns regarding its ability to maintain the appearance and perception
of independence based on the discussion during the July 21 meeting; he indicated that the
proposals from the original competitive selection process were reevaluated, and that based
on the overall assessment, Vasquez & Company LLP was determined to be the next most
qualified proposer and submitted the second-lowest priced proposal.

Council Member Kwan stated that she did not accuse Moss, Levy & Hartzheim LLP of any
wrongdoing and explained her reasons for supporting a different firm, noting that after 11
years with the same firm, she believed it was healthy and responsible to make a change; and
she thanked City Manager Lazzaretto for explaining the process.

Council Member Han explained his reasons for supporting retention of the same auditing
firm, expressed disappointment that Moss, Levy & Hartzheim LLP withdrew, and welcomed
Vasquez & Company LLP.

Mayor Pro Tem Fu thanked Council Member Han for his comments; expressed
disappointment regarding the circumstances that led Moss, Levy & Hartzheim LLP to
withdraw and the additional cost associated with selecting Vazquez & Company LLP; and he
expressed hope that the new firm would provide the same level of professional service.

  5 13  09-15-2026
 In response to Mayor Cheng’s inquiries, City Manager Lazzaretto stated that prior to
withdrawing, Moss, Levy & Hartzheim LLP offered to meet individually with each Council
Member to address any questions or concerns regarding the audit; he indicated that Council
Member Kwan declined to meet with the firm; and he noted that the audit is due by the end
of the calendar year.

Mayor Cheng spoke about the importance of communicating with firms performing work on
the City’s behalf regarding any questions or concerns; and he encouraged Council Members
to meet with these firms when such offerings are made.

Council Member Kwan clarified that she was informed the meeting with the firm was
voluntary; she spoke about the importance of transparency; and she requested that her
decision to not meet with the firm not be characterized as wrongdoing.

Council Member Fu stated that he wanted City Manager Lazzaretto to complete his
comments.

City Manager Lazzaretto indicated that there is email correspondence he would make
available to anyone interested in understanding the nature of his communication with
Council Member Kwan regarding the City’s auditing firm.

Mayor Cheng clarified that the purpose of the meetings with Moss, Levy & Hartzheim LLP
was to address any questions or concerns; and he noted that four Council Members were
willing to meet with the firm.

Council Member Han clarified for the record that he did not meet with Moss, Levy &
Hartzheim LLP; although a meeting had been scheduled, the firm withdrew prior to the
meeting.

Mayor Pro Tem Fu clarified his understanding of the reasons Moss, Levy, & Hartzheim LLP
withdrew; and he disputed the characterization that the firm had publicly stated it was
unable to independently perform the City’s auditing services.

Council Member Kwan questioned whether the firm’s decision to withdraw was based on
information obtained through its meetings with the four Council Members.

Council Member Cao stated that meetings offered by third-party contractors provide Council
Members an opportunity to learn about their work and are voluntary; he clarified that the
Council Members did not meet with the firm as a group; and he noted that Moss, Levy &
Hartzheim LLP had provided auditing services to the City for 11 years because previous City
Councils had continued to approve the firm based on their satisfaction with its services.

  6 14  09-15-2026
 Council Member Kwan spoke about the importance of maintaining her independence as a
Council Member and asking questions on behalf of taxpayers; she stated that a majority vote
does not necessarily mean the best decision was reached; and she requested that her
questions and concerns not be minimized.

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Fu, seconded by Council Member Cao, and carried on a roll
call vote to approve Consent Calendar Item 9.c - Professional Services Agreement with
Vasquez & Company LLP for the City’s financial auditing services.

  b. Resolution No. 7711 establishing fees for City facility use.
  CEQA: Not a Project
  Recommended Action: Adopt

Deputy City Manager Bruno presented the Staff Report.

Council Member Kwan inquired whether the proposed fees would apply to the City’s
Architectural Review Boards (“ARBs”) and Homeowners’ Associations (“HOAs”).

Deputy City Manager Bruno explained that the ARBs and HOAs are separate entities; that
the ARBs perform design review services within their respective HOA areas on behalf of the
City; and that the proposed fees would not apply to the ARBs because they are performing
a City function.

City Manager Lazzaretto further explained that because the ARBs act on behalf of the City,
they would not be required to rent City facilities, whereas HOAs are separate from the City
and would be subject to the applicable facility rental fees.

City Attorney Maurer clarified that fees are not being waived for the ARBs; he stated that the
ARBs are part of the City and the City would not charge itself for use of its facilities.

  7 15  09-15-2026
 Council Member Kwan referenced resolutions dating back to 1968 concerning the
establishment of the HOAs.

Mayor Pro Tem Fu raised a point of order, stating that the discussion was beyond the scope
of the agendized item, and requested that City Attorney Maurer address the issue.

City Attorney Maurer asked Council Member Kwan to clarify her point.

Council Member Kwan referenced an amended resolution from 2012 regarding regulations
for HOAs and ARBs; and she stated that the ARBs and HOAs do not operate separately.

Mayor Pro Tem Fu made a motion to table the discussion on the ARB and HOAs, stating that
the comments had not been connected to the agendized matter concerning use of City
facilities.

City Attorney Maurer clarified that the HOAs and ARBs operate separately; that the ARBs
were established pursuant to the City’s Municipal Code; and he indicated that there was no
discrepancy regarding their distinction.

In response to Council Member Han’s inquiries, Deputy City Manager Bruno stated that the
proposed fees are set at a low-cost recovery level of 0-30% of the City’s costs; that the use of
the three proposed facilities would be limited to nonprofits and Arcadia-based civic
organizations; and that the facilities were being proposed for rental due to increased interest
in their use.

SUMMARY

The Political Reform Act of 1974 (Government Code Section 81000, et seq.) requires
every local agency to review its Conflict of Interest Code (the “Code”) biennially to
determine whether the Code remains accurate and up-to-date or requires
amendments.

As part of the City’s biennial review, amendments to the Code have been identified
as necessary to ensure it accurately reflects the City’s current organizational
structure and designated positions. It is recommended that the City Council adopt
Resolution No. 7714, approving and adopting an amended Conflict of Interest Code
pursuant to the Political Reform Act of 1974.

BACKGROUND

The Political Reform Act (the “Act”) requires all public agencies to adopt and maintain
a Conflict of Interest Code that establishes the rules for disclosure of personal assets
and prohibits public officials from making or participating in governmental decisions
that may affect personal assets. The Conflict of Interest Code must specifically
designate all agency positions that make or participate in the making of decisions

and assign specific types of personal assets to be disclosed, which may be affected
by the exercise of powers and duties of that particular position.

The Act further requires that an agency regularly review and update its Code, as
necessary, when directed by the code-reviewing body or when change is necessitated
by different circumstances (Sections 87306 and 87306.5).

Pursuant to the Act, the City adopted a Conflict of Interest Code that was last
amended and approved by the City Council on October 4, 2022. As the City’s code-
reviewing body, the City Council is responsible for approving amendments to the
Code. Staff has reviewed the Code and has determined that amendments are
necessary to designate new positions, revise disclosure categories and titles of
existing positions, and remove the titles of positions that have been abolished and/or
no longer participate in or make governmental decisions.

Government Code Section 87303 provides that no code or amendment to a code
shall be effective until it has been approved by the code-reviewing body. Attached is
a redline version of Arcadia’s proposed Conflict of Interest Code.

DISCUSSION

While the majority of the positions listed the Code remain accurate, the Code must
be amended to: (1) include new positions to be designated; (2) revise the titles of
existing positions; (3) delete titles that have been abolished; and/or (4) remove titles
that no longer make or participate in governmental decision-making. Attached to
Resolution No. 7414 is a redline version of the proposed amended Conflict of Interest
Code showing the revisions to be made.

Government Code Section 87303 provides that no Code or amendment to a Conflict
of Interest Code shall be effective until it has been approved by the code-reviewing
body. City Council’s adoption of Resolution No. 7714 would satisfy this requirement.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

The proposed action does not constitute a project under the California Environment
Quality Act (“CEQA”), as it can be seen with certainty that it will have no impact on the
environment.

SUMMARY

To comply with state mandated stormwater requirements, the City of Arcadia
became a member of the Rio Hondo/San Gabriel River Watershed Management
(“RH/SGRWM”) Joint Powers Authority (“JPA”), which is comprised of the Cities of
Arcadia, Bradbury, Duarte, Monrovia, and Sierra Madre.

Prior to the formation of the JPA, the City of Arcadia was responsible for processing
invoices and making payments to consultants for the development of multi-benefit
stormwater projects on behalf of the participating member agencies. Following the
formation of the RH/SGRWM JPA, the JPA assumed responsibility for the financial
administration of these projects. Accordingly, the City of Arcadia is no longer
responsible for processing consultant payments and is required to remit its
respective cost-share contribution directly to the JPA.

It is recommended that the City Council authorize payment to the RH/SGRWM JPA,
representing the City of Arcadia’s cost-share contribution toward the fifth
amendment to the current Watershed Management Program agreement with

concept reports, in the amount of $64,824.02.
BACKGROUND

In 2012, the Los Angeles Region Water Quality Control Board adopted the National
Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (“NPDES”) Municipal Separate Storm Sewer
System Permit (“MS4 Permit”), establishing waste discharge requirements for
stormwater and non-stormwater discharges within the watersheds of Los Angeles
County. The MS4 Permit provides permittees with flexibility to achieve compliance
over time through the development and implementation of a Watershed
Management Program (“WMP”) at the watershed scale. The WMP framework allows
participating agencies to implement customized strategies, control measures, and
Best Management Practices (“BMPs”) designed to address watershed-specific water
quality priorities and achieve the requirements of the MS4 Permit.

In 2013, the Cities of Arcadia, Azusa, Bradbury, Duarte, Monrovia, and Sierra Madre,
together with the County of Los Angeles and Los Angeles County Flood Control
District, formed the Rio Hondo/San Gabriel River Water Quality Group (“Group”) to
fulfill the requirements of the Los Angeles County MS4 Permit. The Group established
an Oversight Committee consisting of City Managers or their designated staff, from
each participating city to provide guidance and oversight of the program. A
Memorandum of Understanding (“MOU”) was executed by all agencies for cost
sharing, the development of the WMP, and the Coordinated Integrated Monitoring
Plan (“CIMP”) for the Rio Hondo/San Gabriel River watersheds.

During the initial formation of the Group, the City of Arcadia took the lead on
management of membership payments and consultant contracts for the Group and
its projects, including the CIMP and WMP development. This meant that Arcadia
collected the annual membership payments from participating cities and used the
funds to pay for the Group’s contracts, which were also administered by the City of
Arcadia.

On May 17, 2022, the City Council authorized the City of Arcadia to participate in a
JPA with the cities of Bradbury, Duarte, Monrovia, and Sierra Madre to create the
RH/SGRWM JPA. Due to policy limitations, the County of Los Angeles and the Los
Angeles County Flood Control District could not be a participant in the JPA; however,
both entities continue to enter into project-specific cost-share agreements with the

JPA. With the formation of the JPA complete, responsibility for managing membership
payments and consultant contracts for the RH/SGRWM JPA has transitioned to the
JPA.

DISCUSSION

In July 2020, the City of Arcadia, serving as the lead agency for the consultant
agreements, entered into an agreement with Craftwater Engineering, Inc. to prepare
multi-benefit stormwater project concept reports for the Rio Hondo/San Gabriel
River Water Quality Group. The agreement was amended in April 2021 to revise the
scope of services, and again, in July 2022, to further modify the scope and extend the
term through July 20, 2024. Following formation of the RH/SGRWM JPA, responsibility
for the agreement was transferred from the City of Arcadia to the JPA, with Craftwater
Engineering, Inc.’s consent.

a Total Compensation Study, which will be used to evaluate the City’s compensation
structure and assess how it compares with the regional market for similar public
sector positions. A Total Compensation Study evaluates base salary, specialty pay,
and benefits to provide a comprehensive assessment of the City’s overall
compensation package.

The City received seven (7) proposals and interviewed the top three (3) consulting
firms, all of whom were deemed qualified to complete the study; however, the
proposed cost, experience, and methodical approach proposed by Baker Tilly would
best fit the City’s needs at this time.

BACKGROUND

A Total Compensation Study is typically conducted to gather market information and
assess an organization’s competitive position relative to other employers. This study
provides valuable data to assist the City in evaluating its compensation practices and
making informed decisions regarding employee recruitment and retention.
Additionally, an objective, data-driven overview of the labor-market is important to
have before making compensation decisions in relation to bargaining proposals.

The City completed its most recent Total Compensation Study in 2024. Since then,
the employment market has continued to evolve, including changes in salaries,
benefits, and competition for qualified candidates. Periodic review of compensation
data allows the City to assess its market position and determine whether existing
compensation practices remain competitive and appropriately aligned with the City’s
organizational needs.

Obtaining current market data through this study will provide an important resource
for evaluating employee compensation and informing future decisions. Accordingly,
the City seeks to engage a qualified consultant to conduct an updated Total
Compensation Study.

DISCUSSION

In preparation for upcoming labor negotiations, a comprehensive compensation
study is being proposed to provide the City with current data regarding its overall
compensation position relative to comparable public agencies. The Study will
evaluate base salaries, benefits, and other forms of compensation, thereby providing
a more complete view of the City’s competitive position within the applicable labor
market.

The results of the study will serve as an important tool in preparing for the collective
bargaining process by establishing a data-driven framework for compensation
proposals, identifying potential recruitment and retention needs, and assessing
areas in which the City’s compensation practices may be above, below, or consistent
with the market. With this information, the City can develop informed bargaining
strategies and evaluate compensation adjustments in consideration of both market
competitiveness and long-term fiscal sustainability.

 Executive Summary
Baker Tilly appreciates the opportunity to provide the City of Arcadia with a tailored approach to its Total
Compensation Study. Through our extensive experience providing human resources consulting services
to public sector clients nationwide, we are well qualified to assist the City in evaluating its current
compensation program and developing recommendations that support internal equity, external
competitiveness and the City’s ability to attract and retain qualified talent.

Our team has been providing human resources and management consulting services for more than 30
years and has conducted hundreds of compensation studies for state and local government
organizations. Our specific experience includes pay and benefits market studies across the State of
California, pay structure design, compensation plan implementation, job evaluation and analysis, and pay
policy and practices. Baker Tilly’s public sector focus means the City will be served by professionals who
understand the unique compensation, benefits and workforce considerations facing governmental
organizations in your region.

For the City of Arcadia, Baker Tilly will conduct a comprehensive review of the City’s compensation
program, including base salary, special pays and benefits. We will work with the City to establish
appropriate public peer organizations, collect and analyze market data, evaluate the competitiveness of
the City’s current salary ranges and benefits offerings, identify potential pay compression or compaction
issues, and provide options for appropriate wage and salary ranges. Our benefits comparison will include
employer-paid retirement contributions, longevity and certification pay, educational incentives, specialty
and standby/call-back pay, insurance contributions and leave benefits to support a complete analysis of
total compensation.

Our approach is highly collaborative. We will work closely with the City’s project team throughout the
engagement to establish the project plan, collect and review necessary information, evaluate preliminary
results and confirm the direction of the study. Our recommendations will be data-driven, and our quality
assurance protocols are designed to safeguard the integrity of the market data and analysis. Baker Tilly
takes pride in providing sound results and recommendations that are fair, defensible and practical for the
organizations we serve.

The City will also benefit from Baker Tilly’s experience serving California public agencies, including recent
work for the cities of Laguna Beach, Hollister, Paso Robles, Vernon and other California organizations, as
well as our familiarity with public safety positions and CalPERS-related considerations. Our Southern
California offices provide a local presence, while our national compensation practice gives the City access
to experienced compensation professionals and resources from across the firm.

We look forward to partnering with the City of Arcadia to provide a reliable and comprehensive
assessment of its total compensation program and practical recommendations that align with the City’s
organizational needs, market conditions, budget and long-term workforce objectives. If you have any
questions or require additional information, please contact me by phone at +1 (972) 748 0514 or via email
at jada.kent@bakertilly.com.

 Service approach
Providing our solution to achieve the City’s objectives
The following pages outline our methodology and proposed project scope for the City’s Total
Compensation Study. Our team of Certified Compensation Professionals developed Baker Tilly’s
approach and project tools. We take pride in our ability to provide your organization with sound results
and recommendations that, if implemented, are fair and defensible.

We are confident that you will find our assertions substantiated by the information presented in this
proposal and the comments provided by our references. We look forward to a successful and lasting
relationship.

  Our process is highly collaborative and requires the participation of our clients. We want to leave
  the City of Arcadia with a total compensation analysis that will assist in achieving
  your compensation philosophy, attract and retain qualified workers, and align with
  your organizational needs. To achieve this, we need your input along the way. We encourage
  organizations that are interested in collaborating with Baker Tilly on such a study
  to be prepared for an inclusive process.

Phase 1 – Project Initiation & Current State Review
•  Project Planning. Baker Tilly will meet with the City’s project team to confirm project objectives,
  finalize the work plan and establish the project schedule. Regular status communication with Human
  Resources will continue throughout the engagement.
•  Data collection. Baker Tilly will collect documentation from your organization such as job
  descriptions, organization charts, salary and benefit schedules, the Fringe Benefits Resolution, the
  memoranda of understanding for each of the City’s five bargaining groups (ACEA, AFFA, APCEA,
  APOA and APWEA), and an employee census file. Current job descriptions will serve as our
  understanding of each position in the study.
•  Current State. We will review the City’s existing job descriptions and compensation system to
  understand position duties and responsibilities, organizational relationships, and the current salary
  and benefit structure. This information will provide the foundation for market matching and
  consideration of internal equity throughout the study.
•  Communication Meetings. In addition to project team meetings, Baker Tilly will also conduct
  leadership and employee information meetings to introduce our team and the project process and
  answer questions about the project. We will also distribute a department head questionnaire to your
  leadership team and, if necessary, meet 1-on-1 or in groups to get additional information about any
  specific classification and compensation challenges in their area.
•  Job Evaluation. Job evaluation involves assessing and comparing positions within an organization to
  determine their relative value. We can utilize your existing job evaluation process or implement our
  own. Baker Tilly has a proprietary point-factor job evaluation system called SAFE® (Systematic
  Analysis and Factor Evaluation), which was designed specifically to measure public sector roles. This
  method assigns point values across multiple levels for each compensable factor (shown below),
  resulting in a total score that reflects the internal equity of each position.
  o  SAFE supports the development of a fair and consistent job hierarchy, aligning with the
  requirements of the federal Equal Pay Act. Results will be reviewed and finalized with your
  organization’s project team to establish job hierarchy.

Phase 2 – Total Compensation Market Study
•  Benchmark Positions. Baker Tilly will review the City’s position titles and identify a sample to be
  benchmarked in the market survey. Benchmarks are typically the most common and recognizable
  positions and, therefore, are most likely to yield higher quality and quantity matches. We will work
  with you to ensure the sample includes every level of the organization, most populated titles, law
  enforcement, and leadership roles necessary to achieve the best results.
•  Public Peer Organizations. Baker Tilly will work with your organization to establish a list of
  comparable peer organizations to include in the study. Generally, these organizations will be similar in
  size and the services they provide, and they will have similar roles. These organizations are often
  those from which you lose employees or gain new ones; however, it may be necessary to consider
  public peer organizations similar in size and services but located outside the immediate geographic
  area. Consistent with the RFP, the survey will include up to 14 comparable regional public agencies
  impacting the Arcadia labor market, confirmed with Human Resources during Phase 1.
  o  To represent the private sector in the dataset, we may utilize pay data from the following
  survey sources, as desired: CompAnalyst, Economic Research Institute (ERI), the Bureau of
  Labor Statistics, and/or Pay Factors.
•  Quality Control. Baker Tilly will review and validate survey data to confirm 75% overlap in duties and
  responsibilities, as this is the accepted best definition of a “good” match. Additionally, we require at
  least 3 matches per benchmark position to determine market value.
•  Data Adjustments. Adjustments may be applied to establish consistency in market data comparison;
  to include adjustments for differences in workweek hours, aging the data if it’s not for the current fiscal
  year, and cost of labor adjustments by geography. Controlling these elements means you can trust
  the accuracy of the data result.
•  Market Reports. Baker Tilly will deliver two market reports: 1) demonstrating an aggregate of the
  market minimum, midpoint and maximum for each benchmark and 2) a comparison of your
  organization’s current ranges to the market range. Sample shown below.

Phase 3 – Compression Analysis, Cost Modeling & Administration
•  Pay Compression and Compaction Analysis. Baker Tilly will test the City’s current and proposed
  structures for pay compression and compaction between employees and supervisors and between
  adjacent grades, including the safety series, and will report the positions and relationships where
  compression is present together with options for resolving it.
•  Employee Allocation and Cost Modeling. To this point, the study has focused entirely on the
  position. In this step, we will shift focus to employees, and Baker Tilly will work with your organization
  to appropriately allocate each employee to a title and grade established within the proposed pay plan.
  Next, Baker Tilly will prepare three scenarios for your organization modeling the estimated cost to
  implementation of the proposed plan. These scenarios are intended to define a consistent approach
  for adjusting employee salaries relative to the newly defined pay range for their position. Common
  scenarios include 1) the minimum action needed to adopt the plan, 2) an approach that mimics an
  across-the-board adjustment and 3) an approach that addresses pay compression.

SUMMARY

The California Vehicle Code requires cities to conduct Engineering and Traffic Surveys
every seven years to prima facie speed limits on City streets. The City of Arcadia’s
current Engineering and Traffic Survey, which establishes the posted speed limits
throughout the City, is scheduled to expire at the end of 2026.

To ensure the City receives high-quality professional services at a competitive cost,
the Public Works Services Department (“PWSD”) solicited a Requests for Proposals
(“RFP”) for a new Engineering and Traffic Survey. Following an evaluation of the
proposals received, it is recommended that the City Council approve, authorize, and
direct the City Manager to execute a Professional Services Agreement with Willdan
Engineering for the preparation of the 2026 Engineering and Traffic Survey, in the
amount of $39,800.

BACKGROUND

The purpose of an Engineering and Traffic Survey is to establish speed limits that are
enforceable by radar on City streets. The California Vehicle Code (“CVC”) governs the
requirements and application of the Engineering and Traffic Survey, which are

  89

Page 2 of 5

generally valid for a period of seven years. The City of Arcadia’s current Engineering
and Traffic Survey was adopted in 2019 and is scheduled to expire in 2026.

The CVC defines an Engineering and Traffic Survey as a survey of highway and traffic
conditions conducted in accordance with methods determined by the California
Department of Transportation (“Caltrans”) for use by State and local authorities. The
survey is required to include the following:

  •  Prevailing speeds as determined by engineering measurements;
  •  Collision reports; and
  •  Highway, traffic, and roadside conditions not readily apparent to the driver.

Pursuant to the California Manual for Setting Speed Limits, speed limit
recommendations are generally based on the 85th-percentile speed, the speed at or
below which, approximately 85 percent of observed vehicles travel. Historically,
speed limits were typically established at or below the 85th-percentile speed.
However, subsequent court rulings have affected the methodology used to establish
enforceable speed limits, including circumstances in which the recommended speed
limit may be set at the 85th-percentile speed or rounded to the next higher 5-mph
increment.

Where a roadway segment has an unusually high collision rate that is potentially
related to vehicle speeds or has unusual roadway or roadside conditions not readily
apparent to motorists, the recommended speed limit may be adjusted downward as
permitted by applicable law and guidance.

Because speed limit violations may be challenged in court, the validity and
methodology of the underlying Engineering and Traffic Survey can be subject to
judicial review. Accordingly, it is important that the City’s Engineering and Traffic
Survey be prepared using sound engineering practices, statistically valid data, and
applicable State requirements and guidance to support the defensibility of the
recommended speed limits.

Previously, the City conducted its Engineering and Traffic Surveys using City staff.
However, for the three most recent surveys, completed in 2008, 2014, and 2019, the
City retained the services of professional traffic engineering firms to assist with data
collection, analysis, and preparation of the surveys. The City will continue this

engineering firm helps maintain objectivity in the collection and analysis of traffic
data and avoids the potential perception of a conflict of interest. The three most

challenged in court.

For the 2026 Engineering and Traffic Survey, the City is seeking the services of a

  •  First Ave between California Street and Duarte Road
  •  Second Avenue between Huntington Drive and Duarte Road

Willdan Engineering prepared the City’s two most recent Engineering and Traffic
Surveys in 2014 and 2019 and has provided the City with high-quality traffic

Additionally, having prepared the City’s two previous Surveys, Willdan Engineering is

prior reports, allowing the firm to efficiently prepare the 2026 Survey.

As a value-added service, Willdan Engineering also proposed reviewing three years
of collision data to assist the City in determining whether the provisions of California
Assembly Bill 43, including the authority under California Vehicle Code Section
22358.7 to reduce posted speed limits by 5 mph under specified circumstances, may
be applicable to certain locations within the City. This additional analysis will provide
the City with information to evaluate whether any existing speed limits may be
eligible for adjustment under current State law.

Willdan Engineering’s scope of services will include conducting radar speed surveys;
documenting roadway and roadside conditions; reviewing and analyzing collision
data; analyzing collected speed data to determine the 85th-percentile speeds;
developing recommended speed limits; and preparing a final Engineering and Traffic
Survey report in a format designed to meet applicable legal and judicial standards.
In addition, Willdan Engineering will conduct 24-hour traffic counts at 99 locations on
various arterial and collector streets throughout the City.

  Scope of Services

The Scope of Services for the Engineering Services for 2026 Engineering and Traffic Survey,

  •  obtaining citywide 24-hour vehicle volume counts, conducting radar surveys,

24-Hour Vehicle Volume Counts

B for a two-day period covering a Wednesday and a Thursday during the Santa Anita
Horse Racing Season. With the Santa Anita Race Track holding its fall and
winter/spring meets every Thursday through Sunday from September through
November and end of December to June respectively, the traffic count data will cover
a non-racing and a racing day. The two days shall be averaged for the final volume.

shall include a summary table listing the two-day volumes and the average for each
location, a map with the final volumes shown, and a table comparing the 2019 counts
to the most recent, with the changes. The Consultant shall be responsible for
submitting the traffic volume data sheets and summary in two (2) hard copy booklet
forms and a digital format.

SUMMARY

The Human Resources Department (“HR”) administers a range of sensitive,
confidential, and legally mandated employment functions in support of the City’s
operating departments, including disability accommodation and interactive
processes, leave management, employee relations, confidential personnel
investigations, and other complex employment matters.

Given the specialized nature of certain employment matters, HR periodically requires
supplemental professional expertise to support its internal resources. HR has
identified a need for specialized professional services related to certain confidential
employment matters, and JL Group has the requisite expertise and experience to
provide these services to the City.

Accordingly, it is recommended that the City Council approve, authorize, and direct
the City Manager to execute a Professional Services Agreement with JL Group for an
amount not to exceed $46,000.

DISCUSSION

The Human Resources Department administers a broad range of sensitive and
confidential employment matters on behalf of the City. These responsibilities require

 Professional Services Agreement for Confidential Employment Matters

HR to ensure matters are handled thoroughly, objectively, timely, and in accordance
with applicable federal and state laws, City policies, and established personnel
practices.

Certain employment matters are unpredictable and may require immediate or
continued attention. These matters can arise with little to no advance notice and may
require a level of specialized attention or resources that extend beyond the routine
administration of the City’s Human Resources programs. The circumstances
surrounding these matters can involve substantial records, multiple sources of
information, competing considerations, and issues requiring careful review and
documentation. Engaging an outside professional service provider in these
circumstances provides additional capacity and subject-matter expertise, while
supporting an impartial and comprehensive process.

Additionally, the City has a legal obligation to respond to certain employment matters
in a timely and appropriate way. Prompt attention helps ensure relevant information
is identified and preserved, involved parties have an appropriate opportunity to be
heard, and potential workplace issues are addressed before they escalate.
Specialized professional services provide the dedicated resources necessary to
support the City in meeting these obligations while maintaining appropriate
confidentiality, objectivity, and procedural integrity.

JL Group has previously provided similar services to the City and, through that
experience, has developed a familiarity with the City’s organizational structure,
policies, and operational environment. Based on JL Group’s subject-matter expertise
and prior experience with the City, staff recommends retaining the firm to provide
the specialized support necessary to assist with current confidential employment
matters.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

The proposed action does not constitute a project under the California
Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”), based on Section 15061(b)(3) of the CEQA
Guidelines, as it can be seen with certainty that it will have no impact on the
environment.

SUMMARY

The City’s current contract with its Information Technology (“IT”) Support Services
consulting firm, SDI Presence Inc. (“SDI”), expires on November 30, 2026. In May 2026,
the City issued a Request for Proposals (“RFP”) for IT Support Services and received
six (6) proposals in response. Staff from several departments evaluated the
proposals based on the criteria established in the RFP. SDI Presence Inc. received
the highest overall score.

It is recommended that the City Council award a Professional Services Agreement to
SDI for an initial five-year term, with the option to extend the agreement for three
additional one-year terms. The total cost for the initial 5-year term is $3,106,798.
Each optional extension is proposed to include a 3% annual increase.

BACKGROUND

Between 2015 and 2017, IT Support Services were provided to the City by two
separate firms. During this period, an insufficient level of technical support was
provided, which had a significant and detrimental impact on City operations. The
City’s IT infrastructure was not adequately maintained or updated, resulting in
security vulnerabilities. Additionally, the City’s information technology infrastructure
and systems were not maintained in alignment with generally accepted standards

  139
 Professional Service Agreement with SDI Presence Inc. for IT Support Services
October 6, 2026
Page 2 of 8

and best practices, resulting in an increasingly outdated and unstable technology
environment.

As a result, the City identified a need for enhanced IT support services to provide
greater continuity of operations, improved oversight, and more proactive
management of the City’s technology environment. In September 2017, the City
awarded an IT Support Services contract to SDI Presence Inc. (formerly Scientia
Consulting Group), replacing the previous IT Support Services provider. The
transition was intended to provide greater stability and continuity of support for the
City’s IT systems, while also addressing identified operational and information
security needs.

Following the successful performance of services under the initial interim agreement,
the contract was extended in 2018. Subsequently, in 2019, a five-year IT Support
Services contract, with the option for two additional one-year extensions, was
awarded to SDI through a competitive process.

During the current contract term, the City’s IT infrastructure was brought into
alignment with current standards and best practices, and previously identified
system deficiencies and information security vulnerabilities were addressed.
Improvements were also made to system reliability, cybersecurity, network
performance, and overall infrastructure management. In addition, a more proactive
approach to maintenance, monitoring, and issue resolution was established,
resulting in greater operational stability and continuity of critical IT services. The
enhanced level of support has provided City staff with improved access to timely
technical assistance and has contributed to a more secure, reliable, and sustainable
IT environment.

Although the City has been satisfied with the services provided by SDI, it was
considered prudent to solicit proposals from other qualified firms to evaluate
available service providers and ensure that the City continues to receive high-quality,
effective, and cost-competitive IT services.

DISCUSSION

In May 2026, the City issued an RFP to qualified firms for IT Support Services and
published the proposal in accordance with City Council Resolution No. 7483. The City

The review committee evaluated each proposal based on the criteria established in

SUMMARY

The Fiscal Year 2025-26 Capital Improvement Program Budget provides funding for
the replacement of existing 8–inch and 10-inch sewer mains with 12-inch sewer
mains, along Santa Anita Avenue, between Christina Street and the alley north of El
Dorado Street. The improvements are intended to accommodate future sewer
demand and reduce potential sewer spills.

To obtain competitive pricing and ensure quality service, the City conducted a formal
competitive bidding process for the project. GRBCON, Inc. submitted the lowest
responsive bid. It is recommended that the City Council approve, authorize, and
direct the City Manager to execute a contract with GRBCON, Inc. for the Sewer Main
Replacement Program in the amount of $1,054,543, with a 10% contingency.

BACKGROUND

In 2006, the State Water Resources Control Board adopted the Waste Discharge
Requirements Program for publicly owned sanitary sewer collection systems in
California with more than one mile of sewer pipeline. Under this program, the City is
required to develop and implement a Sewer System Management Plan (“SSMP”).

  147
 Award Sewer Main Replacement Program
October 6, 2026
Page 2 of 4

The SSMP establishes routine preventative operation and maintenance activities
designed to support the City’s goal of preventing sanitary sewer overflows. These
activities include annual inspections, routine sewer main cleaning, repair of damaged
or deteriorated sewer infrastructure, and replacement of sewer mains operating
above their design capacity.

The City of Arcadia’s 2022 Sewer Master Plan Study identified and prioritized
segments of sanitary sewer system that are operating at or above their design
capacity. Several segments along Santa Anita Avenue were identified as inadequate
to accommodate current peak flows. Anticipated development along Santa Anita
Avenue is expected to generate additional sewer flows, further increasing demand
on the system and the potential for sewer backups and overflows.

To address these capacity deficiencies, the existing 8-inch and 10-inch sewer mains
along Santa Anita Avenue, between Christina Street and the alley north of El Dorado
Street, will be replaced with new 12-inch sewer mains. The larger-diameter sewer
mains will provide additional capacity to accommodate peak flows and reduce the
potential for sewer backups.

The project will utilize in-ground pipe bursting to replace the existing sewer mains.
This trenchless construction method will minimize the amount of excavation
required and reduce impacts to traffic along Santa Anita Avenue during construction.
Construction is anticipated to begin in December and is expected to take
approximately three months to complete. A Project Location Map is provided as
Exhibit “A”.

DISCUSSION

A Notice Inviting Bids was published on August 10, 2026, in accordance with City
Council Resolution No. 7483, and bid packages were provided to contractors that
perform this type of work. On September 1, 2026, the City Clerk received five bids
with the following results:

SUMMARY

To enhance the existing water supply infrastructure, Arcadia is partnering with the
City of Sierra Madre to construct a new water supply well within the Arcadia Public
Works Services Department Yard. To ensure the City is receiving the most
competitive prices and quality service for this work, the Public Works Services
Department (“PWSD”) conducted a formal bid process. South West Pump & Drilling,
Inc. submitted the lowest responsive bid.

It is recommended that the City Council approve, authorize, and direct the City
Manager to execute a contract with South West Pump & Drilling, Inc. for the Goldring
Well Drilling Project in the amount of $2,274,647, with a 10% contingency.

BACKGROUND

The City provides water to over 57,000 residents, primarily with water pumped from
the Main San Gabriel Basin, West Raymond Basin, and the East Raymond Basin. To
enhance the existing water supply infrastructure, Arcadia is partnering with the City
of Sierra Madre to construct a new water supply well (Goldring Well) in the Main San
Gabriel Basin.

  168
 Award Goldring Well Drilling Project
October 6, 2026
Page 2 of 5

On November 17, 2020, the Arcadia City Council approved a New Joint Groundwater
Production Well Agreement between the Cities of Arcadia and Sierra Madre to jointly
design, construct, operate, and maintain a groundwater production well in the Main
San Gabriel Basin. Per the terms of the Joint Agreement, Arcadia and Sierra Madre
are each responsible for 50% of the cost of all matters related to the new well.

In March 2023, in response to increased concern over Per- and polyfluoroalkyl
substances (“PFAS”), also known as “forever chemicals”, the Environmental Protection
Agency published proposed regulations that would set Maximum Contaminant
Levels for select PFAS contaminants. PFAS can be found in products such as food
packaging and commercial and household products, which often end up in
groundwater and are toxic at relatively low concentrations, thus, presenting a danger
to both human health and the environment. On June 20, 2023, the City Council
approved an amendment to the agreement to include treatment for the new well to
address PFAS that had been detected in other groundwater sources within the
vicinity of the Goldring Well.

The Goldring Well and PFAS Treatment Project consists of constructing a new
groundwater production well, PFAS treatment plant, 30,000-gallon backwash tank
with a 4-inch diameter sewer pipeline, 12-inch diameter ductile iron water main, and
a 30-inch diameter Reinforced Concrete Pipe (“RCP”) pump-to-waste storm drain
pipeline.

To minimize project costs and mitigate the extended lead time associated with
procuring Ion Exchange (“IX”) adsorption systems, PWSD staff elected to procure the
IX adsorption treatment system separately and provide the equipment to the
installation contractor. On December 2, 2025, the City Council approved a
Professional Services Agreement with AqueoUSVETS LLC for the purchase of IX
adsorption treatment vessels.

The water, sewer, and storm drain pipelines have been constructed. This phase of
the project consists of drilling the Goldring Well. Installation of the well equipment
and PFAS treatment system will be performed through a separate contract. To
ensure the City is receiving the most competitive prices and quality service for this
work, the PWSD conducted a formal bid process.

DISCUSSION

A Notice Inviting Bids was published in accordance with City Council Resolution No.
7483, and bid packages were distributed to contractors that perform this type of
work. On September 1, 2026, the City Clerk received five sealed bids with the
following results:

Bidder  Location  Bid Amount
South West Pump & Drilling, Inc.  Coachella, CA  $ 2,274,647

Best Drilling and Pump, Inc.  Colton, CA  $ 2,348,497

Layne Christensen Company  Redlands, CA  $ 2,414,604

Zim Industries, Inc.  Bakersfield, CA  $ 2,849,396

Nor-Cal Pump & Well Drilling, Inc.  Yuba City, CA  $ 2,868,550

Bid documents and the contractor’s background were investigated. Based on that
review, it has been determined that South West Pump & Drilling, Inc. is the lowest
responsive bidder for this work and is qualified to complete the project as defined in
the bid documents. South West Pump & Drilling, Inc. has successfully completed
similar projects for the Cities of Orange, Tustin, and Big Bear Lake, and the Western
Municipal Water District, Rancho California Water District, and Beaumont-Cherry
Valley Water District.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

Pursuant to the provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”), an
Initial Study/Mitigated Negative Declaration (“IS/MND”) was prepared to evaluate the
potential environmental effects associated with the implementation of the Goldring
Well and PFAS Treatment Project. The IS/MND found that there would be either no
impact or less than significant impact on all resources, with the exceptions of Air
Quality, Hazards and Hazardous Materials, Noise, and Tribal Cultural Resources.
These four resource categories were found to have “Less than significant Impact with
Mitigation Incorporated.”

For 30 days, from February 10, 2025, to March 11, 2025, the Draft IS/MND was
circulated for public review and comments. On April 1, 2025, the City Council adopted
the IS/MND for the Project, approved the Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting
Program, and authorized the execution of the Notice of Determination. On April 3,
2025, the Mitigated Negative Declaration/Notice of Determination was filed with the
Los Angeles County Clerk and was published with the State Clearing House. The CEQA
process has, therefore, been completed.

FISCAL IMPACT

Funds in the amount of $7.0 million have been budgeted in the Fiscal Year 2024-25
Capital Improvement Program for the construction of the new Goldring Well and
Treatment System.

On December 2, 2025, the City Council approved a Professional Services Agreement
with AqueoUSVETS LLC for the purchase of IX adsorption treatment vessels in the
amount of $1,010,801.95. Following this expenditure, $5,989,198.05 remains
available in the CIP budget for the construction phases of the project.

The total cost for the Project is $2,274,647, and with a 10% contingency, the total
project cost is $2,502,111.70. The City of Arcadia’s cost share, including the
contingency, is $1,251,055.85.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council determine that the California Environmental
Quality Act (“CEQA”) process for the Goldring Well and PFAS Treatment Project has
been completed in accordance with CEQA; and approve, authorize, and direct the
City Manager to execute a contract with South West Pump & Drilling, Inc. for the
Goldring Well Drilling Project in the amount of $2,274,647, with a 10% contingency.

SUMMARY

The Public Works Services Department (“PWSD”) is responsible for the care and
maintenance of approximately 15,300 trees located throughout the City, including
trees within City parks, rights-of-way, medians, and public facilities. To ensure the
City receives high-quality professional tree services at competitive pricing, the PWSD
evaluated available contracting options. Following this review, the PWSD determined
that participating in a competitively bid contract through a cooperative “piggyback”
procurement process would provide an efficient and cost-effective means of
obtaining the required services.

It is recommended that the City Council approve, authorize, and direct the City
Manager to execute a contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc. (“WCA”) for annual tree
trimming services, tree removal, and replacement in the amount of $451,547, with
the option of two one-year extensions. It is further recommended that the City
Council delegate the authority to approve future extensions under this agreement to
the City Manager, without having to return to the City Council for subsequent
approval, provided that any changes to the financial terms stay within standard
inflationary limits.

BACKGROUND

The Public Works Services Department is responsible for the care and maintenance
of approximately 15,300 trees located in City parks, rights-of-way, medians, and
public facilities throughout the City. To maintain the City’s Urban Forest, an annual
Tree Trimming Grid Program was created to ensure that all City trees are trimmed
once every four years. This preventative maintenance program provides for the
general upkeep of the existing tree inventory and allows for tree removal and
replacement. The annual tree trimming, removal, and replacement program help
protect residents and visitors traveling on City streets by minimizing the likelihood of
fallen tree limbs due to overgrowth and decay.

DISCUSSION

The City’s purchasing rules and procedures allow the City to “piggyback” onto, or join,
an existing written purchase contract obtained through a competitive bidding
process that is prepared and awarded by another local, state, or federal government
agency. On February 24, 2025, the City of La Verne issued a competitive Request for
Proposals solicitation for Tree Maintenance and Arborist Services.

On June 16, 2025, the City of La Verne awarded a contract to WCA for a five-year
period and has allowed other agencies the opportunity to piggyback and award a
contract at the same prices and terms. Through the piggyback process, the PWSD
was able to procure the grid trimming cost per tree at $100, plus competitive pricing
for other contract items such as emergency crew response, various species of Palm
tree trimmings, large tree removal, and special service request trimmings that may
not be in the annual grid trim area.

PWSD explored possible contract options, and it was determined that piggybacking
on the competitive pricing bid with the City of La Verne would be the lowest cost
option to meet both the City’s annual tree trimming service needs and prevailing
wage requirements, for a total contract cost of $401,547. This contract cost
represents nearly a 2.11% decrease compared to the existing contract amount of
$410,192.40. This decrease is primarily due to lower proposed rates for various tree
trimming services. The table below highlights some of the services with reduced
rates.

Additionally, to prevent damaged and diseased trees from falling and causing
damage, the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Capital Improvement Program Budget includes
$50,000 for the removal and replacement of diseased and decaying trees. The
contract will include annual tree trimming services and tree removal and
replacement for $451,547.

WCA has extensive experience providing tree maintenance and management
services, with more than 40 years of experience in the tree care industry. WCA is the
City of Arcadia’s current tree trimming contractor and has provided the City with
reliable and high-quality services for the past three years. WCA currently provides
tree maintenance services to several Southern California municipalities, including the
Cities of Duarte, Sierra Madre, Glendora, Monrovia, and Temple City.

In addition to performing services under the City’s Annual Tree Trimming Grid and
Tree Removal and Replacement programs, WCA has provided the City with access to
its proprietary tree inventory and management software, ArborAccess. The software
maintains detailed information on more than 15,300 City trees, including tree
species, size, condition, location, and maintenance history. This comprehensive tree
inventory and data management system has been a valuable resource for the PWSD
in assessing the overall condition of the City’s urban forest, responding to service
requests, and documenting information relevant to potential insurance claims.

Improvement Program Budget includes $50,000 for the Annual Tree Removal and
Replacement Program.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council determine that the proposed action is not a
project subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”); and approve,
authorize, and direct the City Manager to execute a contract with West Coast
Arborists, Inc. for annual tree trimming services, tree removal, and replacement in
the amount of $451,547, with the option of two one-year extensions. It is further
recommended that the City Council delegate the authority to approve future
extensions under this agreement to the City Manager, without having to return to
the City Council for subsequent approval, provided that any changes to the financial
terms stay within standard inflationary limits.

   STAFF REPORT
  PUBLIC WORKS SERVICES DEPARTMENT
DATE:  October 6, 2026

TO:  Honorable Mayor and City Council

FROM:  Paul Cranmer, Assistant City Manager/Public Works Services Director
  By: John Corona, Utilities Manager

SUBJECT:  PURCHASE 2,469.99 ACRE-FEET OF IMPORTED CYCLIC STORAGE WATER
  FROM THE MAIN SAN GABRIEL BASIN WATERMASTER IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $2,684,879.13
  CEQA: Not a Project
  Recommendation: Approve

SUMMARY

The City of Arcadia obtains a significant portion of its drinking water supply from the
Main San Gabriel Groundwater Basin (“Main Basin”). The remaining water demand is
met through City-owned wells that pump a fixed quantity of groundwater from the
Raymond Basin. Arcadia maintains a Cyclic Storage Account with the Main Basin,
which allows the City to store supplemental Replacement Water for future use.

The City has an opportunity to pre-purchase imported water made available through
the Upper San Gabriel Valley Municipal Water District (“Upper Water”), at a cost of
$1,087 per acre-foot. This rate is $100 per acre-foot less than the typical cost of
Replacement Water. The purchased water will be used to meet the City’s water
demands during Fiscal Year 2026-27, with any unused water remaining in storage for
future use. By securing water at the lower pre-purchase rate, the City and its
customers are expected to realize savings of approximately $246,999 in water costs.

It is recommended that the City Council approve the purchase of 2,469.99 acre-feet
of Imported Cyclic Storage Water from the Main San Gabriel Basin Watermaster, in
the amount of $2,684,879.13.

  215
 Authorize Purchase of Cyclic Storage Water
October 6, 2026
Page 2 of 3

BACKGROUND

In 1973, an overproduction of water from the Main Basin resulted in a stipulated
judgment that created the Main San Gabriel Basin Watermaster. The Main San
Gabriel Basin Watermaster is a nine-person board appointed by the Los Angeles
County Superior Court that administers and enforces the provisions of the Main San
Gabriel Basin Judgment. This Judgment established water rights and responsibilities
for the efficient management of the quantity and quality of the Main Basin.

This is accomplished, in part, by the Main San Gabriel Basin Watermaster
determining the total amount of water that can be pumped from the Main Basin each
year, free from a Replacement Water assessment; this amount is referred to as the
Operating Safe Yield. The Operating Safe Yield was set at 160,000 acre-feet. The City
of Arcadia’s annual share of the Operating Safe Yield is 4.23%, or 6,769.68 acre-feet.
Pumping more water than the amount established for a given year is allowed;
however, the City must then purchase Replacement Water to recharge the
groundwater basin. For context, one acre-foot is approximately the size of an entire
football field buried in one foot of water.

DISCUSSION

The Main San Gabriel Basin Watermaster has established the Replacement Water
rate at $1,187 an acre-foot for Fiscal Year 2026-27. To encourage water agencies to
purchase available water from the State Water Project, a reduced rate of $1,087 per
acre-foot is being offered for purchases made prior to January 1, 2027. By pre-
purchasing 2,469.99 acre-feet of additional imported supplemental water at the
reduced rate, the City will save approximately $246,999 compared to purchasing
Replacement Water at the standard Fiscal Year 2026-27 rate.

The advantages of pre-purchasing imported supplemental water and storing it in the
City’s Cyclic Storage Account are two-fold. First, it ensures that water is delivered to
the Main Basin, which helps maintain higher groundwater levels than would
otherwise be achieved through the purchase of Replacement Water. Second, the
water is secured at a lower purchase price and may be credited to the City’s Cyclic
Storage account for up to five years, providing additional flexibility in managing
future water demands.

  216
 Authorize Purchase of Cyclic Storage Water
October 6, 2026
Page 3 of 3

Because the cost of Replacement Water is expected to increase annually, pre-
purchasing the imported supplemental water at the current reduced rate will provide
increasing cost savings over time.

ENVIRONMENTAL ANALYSIS

The proposed action does not constitute a project under the California
Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”), under Section 15061 (b)(3) of the CEQA
Guidelines, as it can be seen with certainty that it will have no impact on the
environment.

FISCAL IMPACT

Sufficient funds have been budgeted in the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Water Operations
Budget for the purchase of Imported Cyclic Storage Water. No General Funds are
required for this purchase and pre-purchasing this water at the reduced rate will save
the City approximately $246,999.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council determine that this action does not
constitute a project under the California Environmental Quality Act (“CEQA”); and
approve the purchase of 2,469.99 acre-feet of Imported Cyclic Storage Water from
the Main San Gabriel Basin Watermaster in the amount of $2,684,879.13.

FROM:  Chen Suen, Fire Chief

SUBJECT:  CONTRACT WITH UKG KRONOS SYSTEMS, LLC FOR UKG TELESTAFF
  CLOUD BASED STAFFING PROGRAM FOR A THREE-YEAR TERM, WITH
  THE OPTION TO RENEW FOR THREE ONE-YEAR EXTENSIONS
  CEQA: Not a Project
  Recommendation: Approve

SUMMARY

The Arcadia Fire Department has utilized UKG Kronos Telestaff for more than 20
years to manage daily staffing assignments and for payroll purposes. Telestaff is
configured to administer the Department’s complex staffing policies and rules in
accordance with the Arcadia Fire Fighters’ Association (“AFFA”) Memorandum of
Understanding (“MOU”) and the Arcadia Fire Department Staffing Policy 1040. The
system also automates staffing telephone calls, provides web-based staffing
management, and maintains historical staffing information through its cloud-based
platform.

UKG Kronos Systems, LLC has proposed an initial three-year agreement with annual
increases set at 4%, followed by three optional one-year extensions with a 6% annual
increase. The initial three-year contract has a total cost of $35,934, plus applicable
taxes. If all three optional one-year extensions are exercised, the total cost over the
six-year period will be $77,949, plus applicable taxes.

It is recommended that the City Council approve, authorize, and direct the City
Manager to execute a three-year contract with UKG Kronos Systems, LLC in the
amount of $35,934, plus applicable taxes, with the option for three additional one-
year extensions. It is further recommended that the City Council delegate the

October 6, 2026
Page 2 of 4

authority to approve future extensions under this agreement to the City Manager,
without having to return to the City Council for subsequent approval, provided that
the annual increases remain within the proposed contractual limits.

DISCUSSION

Telestaff is an essential component of the Fire Department’s daily operations. The
platform tracks personnel assignments, vacancies, overtime, leave, shift trades, and
timecard information used for payroll processing. It also applies to the staffing rules
established under Fire Department Policy 1040 and the provisions of the AFFA MOU
when filling vacancies and making staffing assignments. Unlike standard workforce
scheduling systems, fire department staffing requires the system to account for rank,
qualifications, work schedules, leave provisions, overtime rules, and minimum
staffing requirements.

The Department has used Telestaff for more than 20 years, and the system contains
extensive historical staffing and payroll information. Telestaff Cloud preserves this
historical information while providing web-based access and automated telephone
notifications to fill staffing vacancies. Continuing with the existing platform will
minimize operational disruption, data migration concerns, and the substantial staff
time that would be required to configure and implement a replacement system.

UKG has confirmed that Telestaff Cloud and its associated hardware and
timekeeping terminals are proprietary products owned exclusively by UKG and its
affiliates. UKG Inc. and UKG Kronos Systems, LLC are the authorized affiliates offering
these products and services. Based on the proprietary nature of the system and its
ability to administer the Department’s established staffing policies and AFFA MOU
requirements, UKG Kronos Systems, LLC qualifies as a sole-source provider for the
continued use and support of Telestaff Cloud.

The proposed contract provides services for 95 personnel (units) and is billed
annually. The initial three-year term runs from September 2, 2026, through
September 1, 2029, with a total commitment of $35,934. The agreement also
provides for three optional one-year extensions, each with a fixed 6% annual
increase. To achieve the best price possible, several rounds of communication and
negotiations with the vendor to secure a discounted rate and favorable pricing for
the City. This proposed contract provides a predictable cost structure and supports

City Council Payment and Reimbursement Policies
The City Council Protocols and Procedures (“Council Protocols”) are provided to all
